snapshot.text: Q1 FY27 revenue grew 18% to ₹1,248 crore; profit rose 5.9% to ₹82 crore. Use the official figures: S1’s ₹1,428 crore and 35% growth conflict with the filing.
Management maintains FY27 revenue growth guidance of 15–17%; this is a forecast, not a guaranteed outcome.

evidence.quote: For the full year FY27 we are maintaining our revenue growth guidance of 15 to 17 percent.

bull_case.text: A larger order book supports demand visibility, although delivery timing and cash collection remain important.

evidence.quote: Order book stood at ₹3,900 crore as of 30 June 2026, up from ₹3,150 crore a year ago.

bull_case.text: Bharuch could expand capacity materially, while data-centre cables offer another growth opportunity if management’s expectations hold.

evidence.quote: The new Bharuch (Gujarat) plant, adding about 30% to cable capacity, is on track to begin commercial production in Q3 FY27.
Data-centre cables are now about 9 percent of our domestic revenue, and we think that can double in two years.

bull_case.text: Promoter pledging has fallen substantially, reducing this particular shareholder risk compared with last year.

evidence.quote: | Of which pledged (as % of promoter holding) | 4.1% | 6.0% | 11.5% |

bear_case.text: Margins weakened despite revenue growth. Contract resets leave earnings exposed to a delay in recovering higher raw-material costs.

evidence.quote: About two-thirds of our contracts have price-variation clauses, but they reset with a lag of one to two quarters.

bear_case.text: Slower utility payments increase working-capital pressure, although management reports no defaults.

evidence.quote: Yes, receivable days increased from 78 to 96 over the last year.
We are monitoring this closely and have not seen any defaults.

bear_case.text: A ₹46.3 crore GST demand creates uncertainty. Management intends to appeal and expects no material impact; that assessment does not establish the outcome.

evidence.quote: raising a demand of **₹46.3 crore** (including interest and penalty)
The Company does not expect any material impact on its financial position or operations.

open_questions.text: Will copper cost recovery restore margins within management’s stated timeframe?

evidence.quote: which we expect to pass on to customers over the next two quarters.

open_questions.text: Will Bharuch start on schedule, and can collections support remaining spending without materially increasing debt?

evidence.quote: Bharuch capex is ₹620 crore in total, about 70 percent already spent.
Net debt to equity is 0.35 times.
